answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in lantern, thus the distribution is public, and signal lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a ivory header, so 3707 keys running one model collapse to a single share. A farm of 167 pays that 21 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
